facts.cost_for_this_site: Today it costs USD 0 (GitHub Free, public repo). The site is about 6 MB and gets about 80 Google clicks per 28 days, well inside the limits: "Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB." and "GitHub Pages sites have a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month." (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits). A private repo needs GitHub Pro: "GitHub Pro now has a reduced monthly price of $4" (https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/learning-about-github/faq-about-changes-to-githubs-plans). That FAQ dates from April 2020, but the current https://github.com/pricing page source still carries the plan data "pro":{"price":4}. So expect about USD 4/month; whether EU VAT is added on top is not confirmed. Deploys add no Actions cost, even from a private repo: "The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free:" ... "For GitHub Pages" (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions). Verifying the domain (one TXT record at GoDaddy) is free. The domain itself stays a GoDaddy cost, unchanged.

private_repo_on_free_tier.answer: No. On GitHub Free, Pages only works from a public repo. Pages from a private repo needs GitHub Pro (personal account, about USD 4/month) or a paid organization plan. Plans page (https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/learning-about-github/githubs-plans): Free includes "GitHub Pages in public repositories"; Pro adds "Advanced tools and insights in private repositories", including "GitHub Pages". ORDER MATTERS. If the repo is made private while still on Free: "Any published GitHub Pages site will be automatically unpublished." GitHub also says to "remove or update your DNS records before making the repository private, to avoid the risk of a domain takeover" (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/managing-repository-settings/setting-repository-visibility). So upgrade to Pro first, then change the visibility. Going private hides only the code and its history; the website stays public: "GitHub Pages sites are publicly available on the internet, even if the repository for the site is private (if your plan or organization allows it)." The GitHub API shows the repo has 0 forks today, so no public fork would stay behind ("Public forks are not made private.").
private_repo_on_free_tier.quote: If the account that owns the repository uses GitHub Free or GitHub Free for organizations, the repository must be public.

preview_deployments.answer: None built in. Publishing from the main branch puts every push live: the last 8 'pages build and deployment' runs took about 40 to 80 s each. In GitHub's documented custom-workflow flow, the deploy step "is skipped if the workflow was triggered by a pull request" (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site). The official actions/deploy-pages action has a 'preview' input, but its description reads: "Is this attempting to deploy a pull request as a GitHub Pages preview site? (NOTE: This feature is only in alpha currently and is not available to the public!)". A staging copy hosted on Pages would also be public: "To publish a GitHub Pages site privately, your organization must use GitHub Enterprise Cloud." (https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/changing-the-visibility-of-your-github-pages-site). Practical options: preview the static files locally before pushing, or run a separate staging repo/site, which would be public ("Maximum of one pages site per repository").

custom_http_headers.answer: Not supported. The Pages docs offer no way to set response headers. In GitHub Community discussion #54257, Yoann Chaudet, whose GitHub profile reads "Engineering Manager at @github", answered: "We don't support this feature today so a meta tag unfortunately is the only way." (May 2, 2023) and "This is not an area that is being prioritized at the moment unfortunately." (Jul 10, 2024). Live check of https://www.elbcar-detailing.de/ on 2026-10-18: none of Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy is sent. GitHub sets a fixed 'Cache-Control: max-age=600' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'. HSTS on custom domains: not sent (observed), and there is no setting for it. GitHub documents HSTS only for private sites on *.pages.github.io: "We automatically secure every subdomain of *.pages.github.io with a TLS certificate, and enforce HSTS to ensure that browsers always serve the page over HTTPS." What custom domains do get is the redirect: "You can enforce HTTPS for your GitHub Pages site to transparently redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS." (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/securing-your-github-pages-site-with-https). That is on for this site: the Pages API shows https_enforced true, and all http:// URLs return 301 to https://www. Meta tags are only a partial workaround. RFC 6797 section 8.5: "UAs MUST NOT heed http-equiv=\"Strict-Transport-Security\" attribute settings on <meta> elements [W3C.REC-html401-19991224] in received content." W3C CSP3: "The frame-ancestors directive MUST be ignored when contained in a policy declared via a meta element."

apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.answer: Yes. Both names work with DNS staying at GoDaddy, and they already do. No ALIAS/ANAME record and no nameserver move are needed, because plain A records are supported. The setup is four A records for @ pointing to 185.199.108.153, 185.199.109.153, 185.199.110.153 and 185.199.111.153, plus a www CNAME to mashreghal.github.io. AAAA records 2606:50c0:8000::153 to 2606:50c0:8003::153 are optional. GitHub then redirects one name to the other. Live state on 2026-10-18: nameservers ns35/ns36.domaincontrol.com (GoDaddy); all four A records present; no AAAA records (no IPv6); www CNAME mashreghal.github.io; https://elbcar-detailing.de/ returns 301 to https://www.elbcar-detailing.de/. The Pages API shows the certificate approved for both www.elbcar-detailing.de and elbcar-detailing.de (expires 2027-01-08), https_enforced true and build_type legacy (branch main, /). Gap: the domain is NOT verified. There is no _github-pages-challenge-mashreghal TXT record (NXDOMAIN at 8.8.8.8), and the Pages API shows protected_domain_state null.
apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.quote: "To set up an apex domain, such as example.com, you must configure a custom domain in your repository settings and at least one ALIAS, ANAME, or A record with your DNS provider." "If you configure the correct records for each domain type through your DNS provider, GitHub Pages will automatically create redirects between the domains."

serverless_for_form.answer: No. Pages is static hosting only. The docs describe no functions, no region choice and no built-in form handling or form storage: "GitHub Pages is a static site hosting service that takes HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files straight from a repository on GitHub, optionally runs the files through a build process, and publishes a website." GitHub Actions cannot serve as the backend either. The Actions terms say "don't use Actions as a content delivery network or as part of a serverless application" (https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-for-additional-products-and-features). The limits page adds: "GitHub Pages sites shouldn't be used for sensitive transactions like sending passwords or credit card numbers." So the contact form has to keep posting to an outside service (Formspree today). Switching to an EU form processor is a change to the form's target URL and the privacy notice, independent of the hosting choice.

data_protection.dpa_available: Not for this account type. GitHub's customer terms: "The GitHub DPA applies to the processing of data for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise (Unified), GitHub Teams, and GitHub Copilot." (https://github.com/customer-terms). The DPA itself: "This GitHub Data Protection Agreement forms part of the GitHub Customer Agreement between Customer (“You”) and GitHub, Inc., (“GitHub”) covering Your legal entity’s use of the Online Services." The site runs on a personal account (GitHub Free; GitHub Pro would be the same), which is governed by the Terms of Service: "These Terms of Service, together with the GitHub Privacy Statement, represent the complete and exclusive statement of the agreement between you and us." So no Art. 28 GDPR processing agreement is available on Free/Pro. Whether the DPA would cover Pages visitor logs under a GitHub Team organization is not confirmed. data_protection.eu_data_location: No EU hosting or data-location option on Free/Pro. Privacy Statement: "GitHub stores and processes Personal Data in a variety of locations, including your local region, the United States, and other countries where GitHub, its affiliates, subsidiaries, or subprocessors have operations." Transfers out of the EU rely on standard contractual clauses (Commission Implementing Decision 2021/914) and on the DPF. Delivery runs through a CDN. GitHub's subprocessor list, which is written for DPA customers, has the row 'Fastly | Content delivery service | United States | United States'. On 2026-10-18 the live response came from a Fastly cache in Amsterdam (X-Served-By: cache-ams-..., x-github-edge-region: fra, X-Fastly-Request-ID). That is just where the CDN edge sits, not a contractual EU location. EU data residency (GHE.com) exists only for GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users, where "GitHub Pages sites can only be published as private" and public repositories are unavailable. It cannot host a public marketing site.

notable_limits: Site size: "Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB." This site is about 6 MB. (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits; same URL for the next five items)
Repo size: "GitHub Pages source repositories have a recommended limit of 1 GB." The repo including history is about 21.7 MB (GitHub API size 21715 KB).
Bandwidth: "GitHub Pages sites have a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month."
Builds: "GitHub Pages sites have a soft limit of 10 builds per hour. This limit does not apply if you build and publish your site with a custom GitHub Actions workflow."
Deploy timeout: "GitHub Pages deployments will timeout if they take longer than 10 minutes."
Rate limits: "If your request triggers rate limiting, you will receive an appropriate response with an HTTP status code of 429, along with an informative HTML body."

One site per repo, static files only: "Maximum of one pages site per repository". No server code, functions or form handling (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages).

No control over response headers. Every response carries a fixed 'Cache-Control: max-age=600' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' (observed 2026-10-18), so browsers may keep the previous version for up to 10 minutes after a deploy. There is no HSTS on the custom domain, only the 'Enforce HTTPS' redirect.
Support: GitHub Free includes only "GitHub Community Support"; GitHub Pro adds "GitHub Support via email" (https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/learning-about-github/githubs-plans).
facts.migration_effort_from_github_pages:
None: this is the current host and it works. Checked live on 2026-10-18: legacy branch build from main /, custom domain www.elbcar-detailing.de, Enforce HTTPS on, certificate valid for apex and www until 2027-01-08, apex-to-www and http-to-https 301 redirects, DNS at GoDaddy unchanged. Small steps would meet the owner's priorities without leaving:
(1) Verify the domain. Add one TXT record (_github-pages-challenge-mashreghal) at GoDaddy and keep it. About 15 minutes, free. Do this before any plan or visibility change.
(2) Private repo. Upgrade the account to GitHub Pro (about USD 4/month) first, then switch the repo to private. About 10 minutes, no DNS change, and the website output stays the same. A USD 0 alternative: publish from a new public repo that holds only the current site files with a fresh history, and keep the old repo as a private archive (Free allows \"unlimited private repositories with a limited feature set\"). That takes about 1 hour, and the site will be briefly unavailable while the custom domain moves and the certificate is re-issued (GitHub: \"The process may take some time.\"). The internal notes would then live only in the private repo.
(3) Previews. There is no platform feature: preview locally before pushing, or use a separate (public) staging repo.
(4) Form. Replacing Formspree with an EU form service is an HTML and privacy-notice change, with no hosting change.
(5) HSTS and security headers. Not possible on Pages alone; they would need a proxy or CDN in front, or a different host.
risks_or_gotchas: Terms gray zone. This site exists to market a business. AUP section 10 says the primary focus of content posted through Pages "should not be advertising or promotional marketing", and Pages is intended "primarily as a showcase for personal and organizational projects". The site is not e-commerce or SaaS and handles no transactions, so it is not named as prohibited either. No primary source explicitly allows or forbids a local-business brochure site, and the terms send such questions to GitHub Support. These Pages terms apply to every account and I found no plan-specific exception, so paying for Pro does not change this. The ToS add: "GitHub has the right to suspend or terminate your access to all or any part of the Website at any time, with or without cause, with or without notice, effective immediately."

Making the repo private while still on GitHub Free takes the site offline ("Any published GitHub Pages site will be automatically unpublished.") and leaves the custom domain open to takeover. Upgrade to Pro first, then switch visibility.

The domain is not verified today: no _github-pages-challenge-mashreghal TXT record (NXDOMAIN at 8.8.8.8), and the Pages API shows protected_domain_state null. GitHub: "Domain takeovers can happen when you delete your repository, when your billing plan is downgraded, or after any other change which unlinks the custom domain or disables GitHub Pages while the domain remains configured for GitHub Pages and is not verified." Once the repo is private, this hits if Pro is ever cancelled or downgraded. The fix is free: add the TXT record at GoDaddy and keep it ("To make sure your custom domain remains verified, keep the TXT record in your domain's DNS configuration." https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/verifying-your-custom-domain-for-github-pages).

No HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy headers are possible. Header-based security scanners will flag the site. HSTS cannot be added with a meta tag (RFC 6797 section 8.5), and a CSP set in a meta tag ignores frame-ancestors (CSP3). Getting real headers would mean putting another proxy or CDN in front, which brings a DNS change and one more provider to name in the Datenschutzerklärung.

GDPR: GitHub logs and stores every visitor's IP address "for security purposes, regardless of whether the visitor has signed into GitHub or not". No DPA is available for personal Free/Pro accounts; the DPA only covers Enterprise Cloud, Enterprise (Unified), Teams and Copilot. GitHub is active under the EU-U.S. DPF. The Datenschutzerklärung has to name GitHub as the host. Whether GitHub acts as controller or processor for these logs is a legal question for the owner or an adviser; not confirmed here.

Private repo does not mean private site. Everything in the publishing folder stays public. Today TODO.md and README.md stay off the website only because of the Jekyll 'exclude' list in _config.yml (checked live: /TODO.md and /README.md return 404). That depends on the legacy branch build running Jekyll. If the publishing source ever changes (a custom Actions workflow or another host), the exclusions may have to be rebuilt.

No staging step: every push to main goes live in about a minute (last 8 deploys took 40 to 80 s), so a mistake is public at once. The official PR-preview option in actions/deploy-pages is alpha and "not available to the public".
Going private only blocks access on GitHub from then on. It cannot recall copies that were already cloned. The API shows 0 forks today, and GitHub notes "Public forks are not made private."

facts.platform: Vercel (Vercel Inc.): free Hobby plan vs. paid Pro plan

commercial_use_free_tier.quote: Fair Use Guidelines (last_updated 2026-09-14): 'Hobby teams are restricted to non-commercial personal use only. All commercial usage of the platform requires either a Pro or Enterprise plan.' The page lists examples of commercial usage, including 'Advertising the sale of a product or service' and 'Receiving payment to create, update, or host the site'. Terms of Service §4 (Last Updated June 1, 2026, https://vercel.com/legal/terms): 'You shall only use the Services under a Hobby plan for your personal or non-commercial use.' Pricing FAQ (https://vercel.com/pricing): 'Our Hobby plan is for personal, non-commercial use.'

facts.cost_for_this_site:
Pro is required because Hobby is non-commercial only. Cost: USD 20 per month net, about USD 240 per year.

Price (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan): '$20/month Pro platform fee', which includes '1 deploying team seat included' and '$20/month in usage credit'. The pricing page shows Pro at '$20 /mo.'

Included usage: 'Pro includes the lowest capacity tier at no extra cost, with a capacity of 1 million CDN requests and 1 TB of data transfer each month.' A 6 MB site with about 80 Google clicks per 28 days stays far below that, and a contact-form function would use only a little of the $20 credit (my assessment, not a Vercel statement).

Taxes: 'All prices shown are in USD and exclude value-added tax (VAT), goods and services tax (GST), and other applicable taxes.' From https://vercel.com/docs/pricing/taxes: 'We are rolling out collection of VAT, GST, or equivalent for international customers starting on April 1, 2026 for all Vercel products and services where required by law.'
- If 19% German VAT is added (no EU VAT ID on file), that is USD 23.80 per month, or USD 285.60 per year (my calculation).
- With a VAT ID: 'You may have an obligation to self-report VAT under the reverse charge mechanism.'

Billing (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan/billing): 'Can I pay annually? No. Only monthly payments are supported.' Payment is in USD: 'You can pay in any currency so long as the credit card provider allows charging in USD after conversion.' Expect card FX fees.

No extra cost for SSL or the domain: the domain stays at GoDaddy at its current cost. Optional add-ons are not needed. Password Protection costs '$20 per month per protected project', and the free Vercel Authentication already covers previews.

Trial (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan/trials): 'Your trial finishes after 14 days or once your team exceeds the usage limits, whichever happens first.'

private_repo_on_free_tier.answer: Technically yes on Hobby, because the repo belongs to a personal GitHub account (mashreghal). Hobby only blocks private repos owned by a GitHub organization, GitLab group or Bitbucket workspace. This is moot, though: Hobby is not allowed for this commercial site. On Pro, private repos deploy normally. For Pro, the doc says 'To deploy commits under a Vercel Pro or Enterprise team, the commit author must be a member of the team', but that rule applies only to org/group repos, not personal-account repos. Making the GitHub repo private therefore works with Vercel Pro.
private_repo_on_free_tier.quote: 'You cannot deploy to a Hobby team from a private repository in a GitHub organization, GitLab group, or Bitbucket workspace. Consider making the repository public or upgrading to Pro.' And: 'This only applies to commit authors on GitHub organizations, GitLab groups and non-personal Bitbucket workspaces. It does not apply to collaborators on personal Git accounts.'

preview_deployments.answer:
Yes, on all plans, and automatic with the GitHub integration. 'By default, Vercel creates a preview deployment when you: Push a commit to a branch that is not your production branch (commonly main); Create a pull request (PR) on GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket; Deploy using the CLI without the --prod flag.' There are two URL types. 'Branch-specific URL – Always points to the latest changes on that branch'. 'Commit-specific URL – Points to the exact deployment of that commit'. The links also appear in the GitHub PR.

Search engines: 'Vercel adds an X-Robots-Tag: noindex HTTP response header to every Preview Deployment automatically' (https://vercel.com/kb/guide/are-vercel-preview-deployment-indexed-by-search-engines). Exception: 'Vercel omits X-Robots-Tag: noindex when a custom domain is assigned to a non-production branch.'

Access control (https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection): 'Standard Protection is available on all plans', and 'Vercel Authentication is available on all plans'.
- Hobby: 'Hobby users are limited to one collaborator at any one time.'
- Pro: 'Unlimited free Viewer seats', whose read-only access includes the 'Ability to comment and collaborate on deployed previews' (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan).

On all plans, a production build can also be staged and promoted by hand: 'disable Auto-assign Custom Production Domains' (https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/environments).

custom_http_headers.answer:
Yes, on all plans, via a 'headers' array in vercel.json. Each rule has a 'source' pattern, a list of key/value pairs, and optional 'has'/'missing' conditions. It works for plain static files: 'This example configures custom response headers for static files, Vercel functions, and a wildcard that matches all routes.' That covers CSP, Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options and Cache-Control.

Limit (https://vercel.com/docs/limits): 'each rewrite, redirect, or header is counted as a Route', with 2,048 'Routes created per Deployment'.

HSTS is already on by default: 'The default value is strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000 (2 years)' (https://vercel.com/docs/headers/response-headers).

apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.answer:
Yes. The nameservers stay at GoDaddy (today ns35/ns36.domaincontrol.com). Neither ALIAS/ANAME nor a nameserver move is needed; nameserver delegation is only required for wildcard domains.

Steps at GoDaddy:
1. Delete the four GitHub A records for @: 185.199.108.153, 185.199.109.153, 185.199.110.153 and 185.199.111.153.
2. Add one A record for @ with the value shown on the project's Vercel domain card. 'For most projects that value is 76.76.21.21 ... your card may show a different address such as 216.198.79.1.'
3. Change the www CNAME from mashreghal.github.io to the project-specific Vercel target, e.g. d1d4fc829fe7bc7c.vercel-dns-017.com.

In Vercel, add both hostnames and set the apex to redirect to www. That is Vercel's own recommendation and matches today's 301 from apex to www: 'We recommend using the www subdomain as your primary domain, with a redirect from the non-www domain to it.' SSL is automatic: 'Vercel automatically provisions an SSL certificate after DNS verification succeeds.'

A public DNS check on 2026-10-18 found no AAAA, CAA or MX record at the apex, so nothing else conflicts. The google-site-verification TXT record stays as it is. Do not add AAAA records: 'we do not support IPv6 yet' (https://vercel.com/docs/domains/troubleshooting).
apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.quote: 'Yes. You can point an apex domain like example.com to Vercel with an A record, and for most projects the value is 76.76.21.21.' And: 'This is what makes ALIAS and ANAME records unnecessary on Vercel.' From https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-domains/add-a-domain: 'Changing only the website's A or CNAME record at your current DNS provider does not require moving the rest of your DNS records.'

serverless_for_form.answer:
Functions on the free tier: yes, but Hobby is non-commercial only. Hobby includes 'Function Invocations — First 1,000,000', 'Active CPU — 4 CPU-hrs' and 'Provisioned Memory — 360 GB-hrs' per month (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby). On Pro, usage draws on the $20 monthly credit, and after that 'Function Invocations: $0.60 per 1,000,000 Invocations' (https://vercel.com/docs/limits/fair-use-guidelines). No framework is needed: 'For projects without a framework, Vercel creates a separate function for each supported source file in the root api/ directory' (https://vercel.com/docs/functions/quickstart).

EU region: you have to set it, because the default is the US. 'By default, Vercel Functions execute in Washington, D.C., USA (iad1) for all new projects.' Set it in project settings or with "regions": ["fra1"] in vercel.json. The region list has 'fra1 | eu-central-1 | Frankfurt, Germany' (https://vercel.com/docs/regions). 'Hobby plans can select any single region.' Pro allows '5 regions'.

Built-in form handling: none found in Vercel's docs. Vercel instead documents a third-party Formspree integration: 'Formspree is a form backend platform that handles form submissions on static websites.' (https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/cms/formspree). Vercel does not store submissions itself. A fra1 function would have to pass each message to a mail or form provider you choose. Runtime logs 'are stored for 1 hour on Hobby, 1 day on Pro' (https://vercel.com/docs/limits).

Terms of Service: 'We will process the personal information in Your Content, Account Information, and System Data as a data controller or data processor in accordance with Vercel's Data Processing Addendum ("DPA"), which is incorporated by reference, and our Privacy Policy as applicable.'

The DPA (Last Updated March 17, 2026, Effective Date March 31, 2026) defines its scope: 'This Addendum applies to Vercel's Processing of Personal Data as a Processor under the Agreement for Customers who are on Enterprise and Pro plans.'

It includes the 2021 SCCs ('In Clause 17 (Option 1), the 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses will be governed by Irish law.') and the UK IDTA.

Sub-processor list: not confirmed. It is in the Trust Center at security.vercel.com, which refused the automated fetch (HTTP 403).
data_protection.eu_data_location:
Not EU-only. I found no EU-only option for self-serve plans in the docs I reviewed.
- Static files: 'Selecting a Vercel Function region does not impact static files, which are deployed to every region by default.' (https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#regions)
- Functions: can be pinned to fra1 (Frankfurt) or another EU region (cdg1, dub1, lhr1, arn1).
- DPA: 'Customer acknowledges that, as of the Effective Date, Vercel's primary processing facilities are in the United States.'
- Compliance docs: 'Additionally, Vercel may transfer data to and in the United States and anywhere else in the world where Vercel or its service providers maintain data processing operations.'
- Infrastructure: 'The Vercel CDN and deployment platform primarily uses Amazon Web Services (AWS)'.

notable_limits: Hobby (free) is for non-commercial use only, so it is ruled out for this site. Its caps include 'Fast Data Transfer — First 100 GB', 'Function Invocations — First 1,000,000' and 'Active CPU — 4 CPU-hrs' per month. Going over is not billed: 'If you have a free Hobby account, you are limited to the usage caps and cannot purchase additional usage.' Instead, 'you will have to wait until 30 days have passed before you can use the feature again.' (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby, https://vercel.com/pricing)

Pro includes 'a capacity of 1 million CDN requests and 1 TB of data transfer each month' plus '$20/month in usage credit'. Beyond that, usage is billed on demand, e.g. Function Invocations at '$0.60 per 1,000,000 Invocations'. (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan, https://vercel.com/docs/limits/fair-use-guidelines)

Deployments created per day: Hobby 100, Pro 6000. Concurrent deployments on Hobby: 1. In vercel.json, 'each rewrite, redirect, or header is counted as a Route', with 2,048 routes per deployment. (https://vercel.com/docs/limits)

Function regions: 'Hobby | Single region', 'Pro | 5 regions'. The default region is iad1 (USA). Maximum function duration on Hobby: '300s (5 minutes) default and max'. (https://vercel.com/docs/functions/configuring-functions/region, https://vercel.com/docs/limits)
Runtime logs 'are stored for 1 hour on Hobby, 1 day on Pro, and for 3 days on Enterprise accounts'. (https://vercel.com/docs/limits)

Password Protection is 'Available on Pro for $20 per month per protected project ... Not available on Hobby'. Vercel Authentication and Shareable Links are free on all plans. For sharing previews: 'Hobby users are limited to one collaborator at any one time.' (https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection, https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/sharing-deployments)
No IPv6 for custom domains on third-party DNS: 'we do not support IPv6 yet'. (https://vercel.com/docs/domains/troubleshooting)

Billing is monthly only and in USD. 'Only monthly payments are supported.' 'You can pay in any currency so long as the credit card provider allows charging in USD after conversion.' (https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan/billing)

Hobby cannot connect to repositories owned by a GitHub organization: 'Vercel does not support connecting a project on your Hobby team to Git repositories owned by Git organizations.' (https://vercel.com/docs/limits)
facts.migration_effort_from_github_pages:
Low. My estimate is about an hour of setup plus DNS propagation. No code changes are needed, because the site is plain HTML with no Liquid tags.

1. Create a Vercel Pro team and import the GitHub repo. It can be private, since it belongs to a personal account.
2. Set Framework Preset to 'Other' and leave the overridden Build Command empty ('Specify "Other" as the framework preset', 'Enable the Override option for the Build Command', 'Leave the Build Command empty'). Without this, the existing _config.yml makes Vercel auto-detect Jekyll.
3. Keep the internal files unpublished. Add a .vercelignore, or move the site into a public/ folder, because the Jekyll exclude list in _config.yml no longer applies. On the first preview, check that /TODO.md and /README.md return 404.
4. Optionally add vercel.json for headers, regions ['fra1'] if a form function follows, and rewrites (or cleanUrls) for extensionless URLs such as /impressum.
5. Add www.elbcar-detailing.de as primary and elbcar-detailing.de redirecting to www. At GoDaddy, replace the four GitHub A records with the single Vercel A value and point the www CNAME at the Vercel target.
6. Once the domain card shows Valid Configuration and the certificate is issued, remove the GitHub Pages custom domain or disable Pages, delete the CNAME file, then make the repo private.
7. Update the hosting section in datenschutz.html from GitHub to Vercel Inc. (DPF and DPA).

404.html works unchanged: 'Emit a 404.html file to your Output Directory and it will be served as the 404 page when a route does not match any other static file.' (https://vercel.com/kb/guide/custom-404-page)

The Formspree form keeps working unchanged because it posts to formspree.io.

Rollback means restoring GitHub's A records and the www CNAME, as long as Pages is still enabled.
risks_or_gotchas: Do not use Hobby for this site even briefly. Besides the commercial-use ban, Terms §4 says: 'We may shut down and terminate projects or deployments using the Hobby plan without notice for any reason or no reason.' (https://vercel.com/legal/terms)

AI-training clause on Hobby and the Pro trial: 'if you are on a Hobby plan or trial Pro plan, you agree that we may use Your Content to train our artificial intelligence ("AI") and machine learning models, and we may share Your Content with third parties...'. On paid Pro: 'Model Training is not enabled by default'. 'Your Content' includes the uploaded repo files and internal notes. During the 14-day trial, opt out in Team settings or skip the trial. (https://vercel.com/legal/terms)

Wrong framework auto-detection: Vercel's source code detects Jekyll by the file '_config.yml' and then runs installCommand 'bundle install' and buildCommand 'jekyll build'. This repo has a _config.yml but no Gemfile. On import, choose Preset 'Other' with an empty Build Command, or delete _config.yml. (https://github.com/vercel/vercel/blob/main/packages/frameworks/src/frameworks.ts, https://vercel.com/docs/builds/configure-a-build#skip-build-step)

Internal notes could become public. Today the Jekyll exclude list (TODO.md, README.md, images/README.md, fonts/README.md) keeps /TODO.md and /README.md at 404 on GitHub Pages (checked 2026-10-18). Vercel's 'Other' preset 'sets the output directory as public if it exists or . (root directory of the project) otherwise', so those files would be served. Use .vercelignore ('Non-targeted files are prevented from being deployed and served on Vercel.') or a public/ folder, and test on a preview. (https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/vercel-ignore, https://vercel.com/docs/builds/configure-a-build)

Extensionless URLs: https://www.elbcar-detailing.de/impressum currently returns 200 on GitHub Pages (checked). On Vercel, cleanUrls has 'Default Value: false'. If it is enabled, 'Visiting /about.html will redirect to /about', but the sitemap lists .html URLs. Use rewrites to keep both URL forms working. (https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#cleanurls)

A form function would run in the US unless the region is changed: 'By default, Vercel Functions execute in Washington, D.C., USA (iad1) for all new projects'. Set fra1 explicitly. Static files are served from all regions regardless. (https://vercel.com/docs/functions/configuring-functions/region)

Moving the host does not solve the Formspree issue. index.html still posts to https://formspree.io/f/..., and Vercel has no built-in form backend; its docs point to a Formspree integration (https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/cms/formspree). An EU-friendly form is a separate step, e.g. a fra1 function plus an EU mail or form provider.

Data still goes to a US company. Vercel's DPF certification is active and the DPA includes SCCs, but 'Vercel's primary processing facilities are in the United States' (https://vercel.com/legal/dpa). Section 2 of datenschutz.html currently names GitHub Inc. as host and must be rewritten for Vercel Inc. at cutover.

Cost guardrail: 'All new teams have a default on-demand usage budget of $200 (which can be customized)'. Lower it and turn on the hard-limit pause: 'you can optionally configure Vercel to automatically pause all projects with a hard limit'. (https://vercel.com/pricing)

DNS cutover: 'Delete any existing apex A records first, since stale records from a previous host block verification.' Also: 'Always use the value shown in your project's domain card.' That value can differ from 76.76.21.21. (https://vercel.com/kb/guide/a-record-and-caa-with-vercel)

Order matters on the GitHub side. Point DNS at Vercel before disabling Pages, deleting the CNAME file or making the repo private. GitHub warns: 'Domain takeovers can happen when you delete your repository, when your billing plan is downgraded, or after any other change which unlinks the custom domain or disables GitHub Pages while the domain remains configured for GitHub Pages and is not verified.' (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/verifying-your-custom-domain-for-github-pages)

A preview on a custom domain (e.g. staging.elbcar-detailing.de) can be indexed: 'Vercel omits X-Robots-Tag: noindex when a custom domain is assigned to a non-production branch.' Keep using the *.vercel.app preview URLs, or add noindex yourself. (https://vercel.com/kb/guide/are-vercel-preview-deployment-indexed-by-search-engines)

VAT and currency: VAT has been collected since April 1, 2026, based on the billing address. Add an EU VAT ID if one exists, so the reverse charge applies. The card is charged in USD, so FX fees may apply. (https://vercel.com/docs/pricing/taxes, https://vercel.com/docs/plans/pro-plan/billing)

facts.platform: Azure Static Web Apps (Microsoft), Free plan vs Standard plan

commercial_use_free_tier.quote: Pricing page FAQ: 'Free tier is intended for hobby/personal usage and does not come with SLA. It is suitable for those looking to explore Azure Static Web Apps. Standard tier is intended for general purpose production workloads and comes with SLA.' The same page's table header reads 'Free (For hobbies/personal projects)' vs 'Standard (For general purpose production app)'. The plans page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/plans) labels the columns 'Free plan (For personal projects)' and 'Standard plan (For production apps)'. I found no sentence that explicitly forbids or explicitly allows commercial use on the pricing, plans or quotas pages, or in the readable part of the Azure Product Terms (https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/terms/productoffering/MicrosoftAzure/MCA). Microsoft states Free is intended for hobby and personal use, which is weaker than a contractual ban.

facts.cost_for_this_site:
Free plan: EUR 0 per month. The Azure account page lists Static Web Apps as 'Always' free with '100 GB bandwidth per subscription, 2 custom domains and .5 GB storage per app' (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/purchase-options/azure-account). The repo has 111 tracked files, about 5.4 MB (checked with git ls-files). The Free limits are 'Storage (single environment) | 250 MB' and 'File count | 15,000' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/quotas). At about 80 visits a month, bandwidth stays far below 100 GB: even 1,000 visits that each loaded the whole 5.4 MB would be about 5.4 GB.

Standard plan, which Microsoft designates 'For production apps': EUR 7.9197 (USD 9.00) per app per month in West Europe. Source is Microsoft's Retail Prices API record {"productName": "Static Web Apps", "skuName": "Standard", "meterName": "Standard App", "unitOfMeasure": "1/Month", "retailPrice": 7.9197 EUR / 9.0 USD, "armRegionName": "westeurope", "location": "EU West"} (https://prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices?$filter=contains(productName,'Static Web')). It includes 100 GB; beyond that, 'Standard Bandwidth Usage' is 0.176 EUR (0.20 USD) per '1 GB' from tierMinimumUnits 100. Pricing page: 'Standard plans are billed on a per hour basis.' The pricing page renders the amounts in JavaScript ('$-'), so the figures come from the API.

Optional costs:
- Azure DNS, only if the nameservers move away from GoDaddy: 'Public Zone' USD 0.50 / EUR 0.44 and 'Public Queries' USD 0.40 / EUR 0.352 per 1M (Retail Prices API). Pricing page wording: 'First 25 hosted DNS zones $- per zone per month' (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/dns/).
- Managed Functions for a contact form: the pricing page says APIs come 'at Azure Functions Consumption plan rates' and 'with 1 million free executions'. The account page lists 'Azure Functions 1 million requests' as 'Always' free, so a handful of form submissions should cost nothing.
- An email-sending service for that form would be billed separately; its price was not verified (the Retail Prices API rate-limited the lookup).
- GitHub side: deploys from a private repo use GitHub Free's 2,000 Actions minutes per month.

Signing up needs 'a phone number, a credit card or a debit card (non-prepaid), and a Microsoft account or a GitHub account'. Per Microsoft, these are used for identity verification and nothing is charged at signup.

Evidence files:

private_repo_on_free_tier.answer: Yes. GitHub integration is part of the Free plan (plans page row 'GitHub integration | ✔ | ✔'), and Microsoft's pull-request doc explicitly assumes private repos (see quote). How it works: the portal adds a workflow ('The GitHub action generates the configuration file and is stored in the .github/workflows folder, named using the following format: azure-static-web-apps-<RANDOM_NAME>.yml.') and deploys with 'an Azure deployment token (recommended), or a GitHub access token' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/build-configuration). The GitHub-side catch: on a private repo the workflow uses the account's Actions quota. 'For private repositories, each GitHub account receives a quota of free minutes, artifact storage, and cache storage for use with GitHub-hosted runners, depending on the account's plan.' GitHub Free gets '500 MB' artifact storage and '2,000' minutes per month, and 'If your account does not have a valid payment method on file, usage is blocked once you use up your quota.' (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions). The SWA quotas page adds: 'When you create an Azure Static Web Apps site, GitHub stores the artifacts for your site even after deployment.'
private_repo_on_free_tier.quote: Anyone can access the staged versions of your application via their URL, even if your GitHub repo is private.

preview_deployments.answer: Yes, built in for GitHub Actions deployments. Each pull request against the production branch gets its own pre-production environment, and a GitHub bot comments the URL ('https://<SUBDOMAIN-PULL_REQUEST_ID>.<AZURE_REGION>.azurestaticapps.net'). 'Once the pull request is closed, the pre-production environment is automatically deleted.' There are also stable branch environments ('published at a stable URL that includes the branch name') and named environments (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/preview-environments). Limits and caveats: Free allows 3 ('Preview environments | 3 | 10' for Free vs Standard, quotas page). Previews are public: 'Anyone can access the staged versions of your application via their URL, even if your GitHub repo is private.' Password protection ('You can use a password to protect your app's pre-production environments or all environments.') has the prerequisite 'An existing static web app in the Standard plan.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/password-protection). Further caveats: 'Custom domains do not work with preview environments.', 'Pre-production environments aren't geo-distributed.', and 'Only GitHub Actions deployments support pre-production environments.' What happens when a 4th PR opens on Free is not documented in the pages reviewed (not confirmed).

custom_http_headers.answer: Yes, including on Free, through staticwebapp.config.json. 'The globalHeaders section provides a set of HTTP headers applied to each response, unless overridden by a route header rule, otherwise the union of both the headers from the route and the global headers is returned.' Each route can also set its own 'headers' (the doc's example sets Cache-Control for /images/*), and 'To remove a header, set the value to an empty string'. The doc's sample config puts 'content-security-policy' in globalHeaders. Restrictions: 'Max file size is 20 KB' and 'Global headers do not affect API responses.' The same file handles: 'responseOverrides', needed for a custom 404 (the doc example rewrites 404 to '/404.html'); redirects ('Default response code is a 302 (temporary redirect), but you can override with a 301'); and 'trailingSlash'. Only some sections are Standard-only: 'Networking configuration is only available in the Azure Static Web Apps Standard plan.' and 'Forwarding gateway configuration is only available in the Azure Static Web Apps Standard plan.' Without a build step: 'Make sure you have your staticwebapp.config.json file copied as well into the output directory.' (build-configuration doc).

apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.answer:
Yes, both work with DNS staying at GoDaddy and no nameserver move. GoDaddy cannot do an ALIAS record, so the apex uses one of two documented workarounds.

www: add a CNAME 'www' pointing to <app>.azurestaticapps.net. Azure validates it via the CNAME: 'Azure validates that the CNAME record was created correctly and is available in the global DNS system. Propagation depends on the time to live (TTL) for your domain and may take several days.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/custom-domain-external). For a zero-downtime switch, validate first with a TXT record at '_dnsauth.<SUBDOMAIN>.<YOUR-DOMAIN.COM>' (custom-domain doc).

Apex option A, forwarding at GoDaddy: Microsoft's option 'Forward the apex domain to the www subdomain'. GoDaddy says 'Forwarding over HTTPS is now automatically applied to your domain when you set up forwarding following these steps.' and 'Adding forwarding will automatically update and lock your @ A record.' You can choose 301 or 302 (https://www.godaddy.com/help/forward-my-godaddy-domain-12123). The apex is never added to SWA, so only 1 of the 2 Free custom domains is used.

Apex option B, A record: point @ at the app's 'stableInboundIP' and add a TXT record at @ to prove ownership. Microsoft describes that IP as 'the IP address of your regional Static Web Apps host', notes that 'If the IP address changes, a CNAME entry is still valid, unlike A record', and warns the apex loses global distribution. Then set www as the default domain: 'When you designate a custom domain as your app's default domain, requests to other domains are automatically redirected to the default domain.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/custom-domain-default). This uses both Free custom-domain slots.

Nameserver move, only if a true ALIAS apex is wanted: Microsoft says 'Some registrars like GoDaddy don't support domain records that affect how you configure your apex domain. Consider using Azure DNS with these registrars to set up your apex domain.' Azure DNS costs USD 0.50 / EUR 0.44 per zone per month plus queries, and every record, including mail (MX), would have to move.

TLS: 'Free SSL/TLS certificates are automatically created for the autogenerated domain name and any custom domains you may add.' Propagation: 'Apex domain changes can take up to 72 hours to propagate.'

GoDaddy's own blog (2026-09-03, 'Beyond CNAME Flattening') says 'GoDaddy's Managed DNS supports SVCB and HTTPS records in full-service mode today'. Microsoft's SWA docs do not list HTTPS/SVCB records as an apex method, so that route is not confirmed.
apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.quote: Some domain registrars (like Google and GoDaddy) don't allow you to point the apex domain to an existing URL. If your registrar doesn't support ALIAS or ANAME records, or doesn't allow CNAME flattening, consider the following options: [Configure your domain with Azure DNS / Forward the apex domain to the www subdomain / Use an A record]. Using an A record directs your traffic to a single regional host of your static web app. When enabled, your static web app no longer benefits from its global distribution, and this may affect your application performance.

serverless_for_form.answer:
Functions on Free: yes. 'Bring your own APIs is only available in the Azure Static Web Apps Standard plan. Built-in, managed Azure Functions APIs are available in all Azure Static Web Apps plans.' Constraints:
- 'Triggers and bindings are limited to HTTP.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/apis-functions)
- 'The maximum duration of each API request 45 seconds.'
- The route prefix must be /api, served same-origin 'without requiring custom CORS rules'.
- No managed identity and no Key Vault references.
- Runtimes are chosen with apiRuntime. The configuration doc lists node:20, node:22, python:3.9-3.11 and dotnet-isolated 8.0/9.0/10.0; older versions have end dates, e.g. 'Node.js 18.x | Linux | 4.x | node:18 | May 31, 2025'.
- Secrets go in application settings, which 'Are encrypted at rest' and 'Are available as environment variables to the backend API'.

Region: 'Azure Static Web Apps is a global service. Your app's static assets are globally distributed. When you create your app, you select a region where the managed Azure Functions app is deployed.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/faq). The docs do not publish the list of selectable regions. West Europe exists as a Static Web Apps region in Microsoft's Retail Prices API (armRegionName 'westeurope', location 'EU West'). A Microsoft contributor on the official repo wrote: 'Static Web Apps is a global service. Only the managed functions and staging environments are localized.' (https://github.com/Azure/static-web-apps/issues/1389). So West Europe for the function is likely, but not confirmed from documentation.

Built-in form handling: none found in the SWA docs reviewed. You would write an HTTP function that receives the POST and forwards it, for example by email. SWA itself stores nothing; where the submission ends up depends on the mail service chosen. In-Azure option: Azure Communication Services, where 'Selecting the Europe geography or one of the country geographies that are part of the EU Data Boundary ensures that your Customer Data and pseudonymized personal data is stored and processed in the EU Data Boundary, aside from specific residual transfers' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/eudb/eu-data-boundary-configure-azure-nonregional-services). Its price was not verified. Logging: 'Logs are only available if you add Application Insights.' Cost: 'Customers can add integrated serverless APIs implemented with Azure Functions to their Azure Static Web Apps resources at Azure Functions Consumption plan rates.' (pricing page).

data_protection.company_and_hq: Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, Washington, USA (DPF list entry: 'Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, WA'). For EMEA customers the Azure billing entity is the Irish subsidiary: 'For EMEA, the billing entity is Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited (MIOL).' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/understand/mca-understand-your-invoice). The DPA adds: 'Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited is Microsoft's data protection representative for the European Economic Area and Switzerland.'

data_protection.dpa_available:
Yes, and it applies automatically with no separate signature. The document is the Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum ('Last updated May 22, 2026'). Key wording:
- 'The DPA is incorporated by reference into the Product Terms and other Microsoft agreements.'
- 'Microsoft makes the commitments in this DPA to all Customers with an existing Customer's agreement.'
- Transfers: 'All transfers of Customer Data, Professional Services Data, and Personal Data out of the European Union, European Economic Area, United Kingdom, and Switzerland to provide the Products and Services are subject to the terms of the 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses implemented by Microsoft.'
- 'Microsoft makes the commitments in these GDPR Terms, to all customers effective May 25, 2018.'
- 'Customer and Microsoft agree that Customer is the controller of Personal Data and Microsoft is the processor of such data'.
The EU Model Clauses page lists 'Azure and Azure Government' as in scope. Download: https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/docs/documents/download/MicrosoftProductandServicesDPA(WW)(English)(May2026)(CR).docx (text extract: [local evidence file, not kept]).
data_protection.eu_data_location:
Static site content: EU-only hosting is NOT CONFIRMED, and the evidence points to global hosting.
- The FAQ says 'Azure Static Web Apps is a global service. Your app's static assets are globally distributed.'
- Microsoft's products-by-region data lists 'Azure App Service Static Web Apps' (SKUs 'Static Web Apps Free' and 'Static Web Apps Standard') with RegionName 'Non Regional'.
- EU Data Boundary scope: 'For Azure, regional services that a customer deploys in an EU Data Boundary region will be in-scope for the EU Data Boundary.' Non-regional services count only if Microsoft names them.
- Static Web Apps is not named on Microsoft's EUDB page for non-regional services (updated 2026-10-16). The EUDB transfer and exception pages and the EUDB change log contain no 'Static Web' mention.
- It is also absent from the Product Terms EU Data Boundary Services list. That list's Azure row covers 'Azure services that enable deployment in a region within the EU Data Boundary' plus named non-regional services.
- The DPA's EU-storage promise applies only 'For EU Data Boundary Services'.

Managed Functions and staging/preview environments run in the region picked at creation, for example West Europe. Preview URLs contain the region, and 'Pre-production environments aren't geo-distributed.'

Any processing outside the EU is covered contractually by the DPA's 2021 SCCs and Microsoft's active DPF certification.

notable_limits: Bandwidth on Free: 100 GB per month per subscription with no overage ('Included bandwidth (per month) | 100 GB'; 'Overage bandwidth | Unavailable'). Pricing FAQ: 'In the free plan if your site exceeds the 100 GB quota, we will not be able to serve your site.' Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/quotas and https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/app-service/static/
Storage on Free: 'Storage (single environment) | 250 MB', 'Total storage (all environments) | 500 MB', 'File count | 15,000' (quotas page). This site uses about 5.4 MB in 111 files.
Custom domains on Free: 2 per app ('Custom domains | 2', quotas; '2 per app', plans and pricing). For Standard the docs disagree: plans and pricing say 5 per app, the quotas page says 6.
Preview environments: 'Preview environments | 3 | 10' (Free | Standard). They are public, have no custom domains, are not geo-distributed, and are GitHub Actions only.
Apps per subscription on Free: 'Apps | 10'. Request size: 'Request Size Limit | 30 MB'. staticwebapp.config.json: 'Max file size is 20 KB'.

Managed Functions: 'Triggers and bindings are limited to HTTP.' 'The maximum duration of each API request 45 seconds.' No managed identity or Key Vault references. Bring-your-own Functions or other backends require Standard (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/apis-overview).

Not on Free: SLA ('Service Level Agreement (SLA) | None'), private endpoints ('Private endpoint | Unavailable'), IP restrictions ('Allowed IP range restrictions | Unavailable'), password protection (prerequisite 'An existing static web app in the Standard plan.'), and formal support (plans page, 'Select Standard when: ... You require formal customer support.').
Builds: 'By default, the app and API builds are limited to 15 minutes.' This does not matter for a site with no build step.

GitHub side, private repo: GitHub Free includes 2,000 Actions minutes and 500 MB artifact storage per month, and 'If your account does not have a valid payment method on file, usage is blocked once you use up your quota.' (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions)
facts.migration_effort_from_github_pages:
Low to moderate. My estimate is a few hours of hands-on work plus DNS wait time. Microsoft says CNAME validation 'may take several days' depending on TTL, and 'Apex domain changes can take up to 72 hours to propagate.'

1. Create an Azure account. Signup needs a phone and a credit or debit card for identity verification. Use pay-as-you-go: a 30-day 'Azure free account' that is not converted ends with 'your account and services will be disabled'. Then create a Static Web App on the Free plan, choose a region such as West Europe for functions and staging, and connect GitHub. You may need to grant the 'Azure Static Web Apps' OAuth app. Azure commits '.github/workflows/azure-static-web-apps-<RANDOM_NAME>.yml' and a deployment-token secret.

2. There is no build step, so per the build-configuration doc: 'Set app_location to the location the files you want to deploy', 'Set skip_app_build to true', and 'Set output_location to an empty string'.

3. Repo-specific issue, checked in C:\Claude_Code_Projects\ElbCarDetailing: GitHub Pages currently runs Jekyll (there is a _config.yml and no .nojekyll). Jekyll's 'exclude' list keeps TODO.md, README.md, images/README.md and fonts/README.md off the live site. SWA with skip_app_build publishes the app_location folder as-is, so those notes would become public. Move the site files into a subfolder used as app_location, or move the notes out. _config.yml and CNAME would otherwise also be published (harmless).

4. Add staticwebapp.config.json, copied into the output folder:
   - responseOverrides 404 rewriting to '/404.html', since GitHub Pages serves 404.html automatically;
   - globalHeaders for security headers.
   Internal links and the sitemap already use explicit .html URLs, which SWA's default rules serve with 200 and no redirect.

5. Review on the <app>.azurestaticapps.net URL and with a test pull request preview.

6. Change DNS at GoDaddy:
   - Pre-validate www with a TXT record at _dnsauth.www.elbcar-detailing.de (Microsoft's zero-downtime method).
   - Switch the www CNAME from GitHub to <app>.azurestaticapps.net.
   - Replace the four GitHub apex A records with GoDaddy forwarding (301 to https://www.elbcar-detailing.de), or with an A record to stableInboundIP plus a TXT record.
   - Set www as the default domain so the azurestaticapps.net hostname redirects to it.

7. After cutover, turn off GitHub Pages and make the repo private.

The Formspree form keeps working unchanged because it posts to an external endpoint. Replacing it with a managed Function is a separate piece of work.
risks_or_gotchas: Microsoft positions Free as non-production. The plans page heads its columns 'Free plan (For personal projects)' vs 'Standard plan (For production apps)' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/plans), and the pricing FAQ says 'Free tier is intended for hobby/personal usage and does not come with SLA.' No explicit ban on commercial use was found, but a business site on Free goes against the stated intent. Standard costs EUR 7.92 (USD 9.00) per month.

Previews are public on Free: 'Anyone can access the staged versions of your application via their URL, even if your GitHub repo is private.' Hiding them behind a password needs Standard. This matters if unreleased content or prices are previewed.

GoDaddy has no ALIAS, ANAME or CNAME flattening (Microsoft: 'Some domain registrars like GoDaddy and Squarespace (formerly Google) don't support these DNS records.'). The apex therefore needs GoDaddy forwarding, which makes GoDaddy's forwarding service handle apex requests, or an A record to one regional IP, which loses global distribution and breaks if 'the IP address changes'. The only other option is moving DNS to Azure DNS.

EU-only hosting is not confirmed. Static assets are 'globally distributed'. Static Web Apps is 'Non Regional' in Microsoft's region data and is not named in Microsoft's EU Data Boundary documentation or the Product Terms EU Data Boundary list. Transfers are covered by SCCs and DPF, but 'hosted in the EU' cannot be claimed in the privacy policy.

Azure account lifecycle: signup needs a phone and a credit or debit card. A 30-day Azure free account that is not moved to pay-as-you-go ends with 'If you don't, your account and services will be disabled.' (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/purchase-options/azure-account). That would take the site offline, so use pay-as-you-go from the start; SWA Free stays EUR 0.

Repo-specific: the Jekyll 'exclude' list in _config.yml (TODO.md, README.md, images/README.md, fonts/README.md) only works on GitHub Pages. With SWA's skip_app_build those files would be deployed and public unless the site moves into a subfolder.
Hard stop at 100 GB per month on Free ('we will not be able to serve your site'). Unlikely at this traffic, but it is an outage rather than a bill.

The default <app>.azurestaticapps.net hostname stays reachable as duplicate content until a default custom domain is set ('requests to other domains are automatically redirected to the default domain').

Managed Functions need upkeep: runtime versions have end-of-support dates in the configuration doc (e.g. 'Node.js 18.x ... May 31, 2025'). They are HTTP-only with a 45-second limit, and SWA has no built-in form feature, so a function plus a mail provider would have to be built and maintained.
Microsoft does retire SWA offerings: the plans page shows 'Dedicated plan (Retired effective October 31st, 2025)'.
On a private repo every deploy, including PR previews, uses GitHub Actions minutes: 2,000 per month on GitHub Free, and usage is blocked without a payment method once the quota is used up.
Free allows only 3 preview environments. What happens when a 4th pull request opens is not documented in the pages reviewed (not confirmed).

facts.cost_for_this_site:
$0 on the Free plan is possible. The limit comes from the number of production deploys, not from traffic.

Plan facts:
- Free plan: "$0/month, forever, for 300 credits/month with a hard limit and no auto recharge option." (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/accounts-and-billing/billing/billing-for-credit-based-plans/credit-based-pricing-plans/)
- Credit costs (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/accounts-and-billing/billing/billing-for-credit-based-plans/how-credits-work/):
  - "each successful production deploy consumes 15 credits"
  - "Bandwidth consumes 20 credits per GB used"
  - "Web requests use 2 credits per 10 thousand (10,000) requests."
  - "Netlify's web forms service is free and unlimited for all credit-based plans."
  - Previews: "Deploy Previews or branch deploys | 0 credits"

My estimate for this site (not a vendor figure):
- The repo serves about 5.4 MB. A full home-page visit is roughly 0.5-2 MB, of which 0.85-1.8 MB are lazy-loaded WebP images.
- Assuming at most about 500 visits a month (the ~80 Google clicks plus direct, WhatsApp and bot traffic), traffic costs about 10-40 credits a month.
- That leaves room for roughly 17-19 production deploys a month on Free.
- The main branch received 54 commits in April 2026 and 18 so far in October 2026. A month where every push deploys would go over 300 credits and pause the site.

Ways to stay on Free:
- Batch changes through pull requests. Deploy Previews are free; only the merge costs 15 credits.
- Put [skip netlify] in commit messages that should not deploy.
- Lock auto-publishing: "only published production deploys will still cost 15 credits".

If that discipline is not realistic:
- Personal plan: "$9/month for 1,000 credits/month, with an auto recharge option (500 credits for $5)". That is about 60 deploys a month. Auto recharge is off by default.
- Pro plan ("Starts at $20/month for 3,000 credits") is only needed for an EU function region, password-protected previews or extra team members.

Other costs:
- DNS stays at GoDaddy, so there is no Netlify domain cost.
- Payment: "Netlify accepts credit cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay." VAT handling for a German business: not confirmed.

private_repo_on_free_tier.answer:
Yes. Private repositories owned by a personal GitHub account deploy on every plan, including Free. Only private repositories owned by a GitHub organization need Pro: the plans table lists "Organization-owned private repos | N/A | N/A | ✓" for Free / Personal / Pro.

One condition applies. Netlify's Deploy Request Policy "only builds and deploys changes pushed to private repositories from recognized authors". Free and Personal cannot add Git Contributors ("Git Contributors* can commit to project through private repositories | N/A | N/A | ✓"), so pushes must come from the owner's own GitHub account.

- Signing up with GitHub links that account automatically: "If you signed up for Netlify using GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket, then your Netlify user will already be linked to that Git provider."
- A commit from an unrecognized identity waits as "Pending approval". The owner can then match it to the existing team member.
- "Note that known bots like Renovate or Claude will not count as a Git contributor."

Sources: https://docs.netlify.com/manage/accounts-and-billing/billing/billing-for-credit-based-plans/credit-based-pricing-plans/ and https://docs.netlify.com/deploy/deploy-overview/#deploy-permissions
private_repo_on_free_tier.quote: Netlify supports the following types of repositories: - private or public repositories owned by personal user accounts - public repositories owned by an organization account - private repositories owned by an organization account (This feature is available on Core Pro and Enterprise plans, depending on Git provider.)

preview_deployments.answer:
Yes. Previews are unlimited on Free and cost 0 credits.

- How they are built: "When you open a pull / merge request in a connected site repository from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or Cursor Origin, Netlify automatically builds a Deploy Preview for you." Each preview lives at deploy-preview-<PR number>--<project>.netlify.app, and every deploy also gets a permanent link.
- Branch deploys are also free ("Deploy Previews or branch deploys | 0 credits"). Visits to previews still count toward web-request and bandwidth credits.
- Who can see them: "Previews stay private unless you change the preview visibility setting." and "On a Free and Personal plan, private projects can only be seen by the Team Owner."
- Sharing a preview with someone else (for example the studio owner) on Free means setting preview visibility to public. Password protection is "only available on Pro".
- Netlify's own pages disagree on Reviewers. The roles doc says "you must have a Pro plan or higher to invite someone with the Reviewer role", while the pricing FAQ says Reviewers are available "With any plan".

See also https://docs.netlify.com/manage/security/secure-access-to-sites/project-visibility/

custom_http_headers.answer:
Yes, on all plans including Free: "Save a plain text file called `_headers` to the publish directory of your site." Alternatively, use [[headers]] tables in netlify.toml. Paths can contain wildcards and placeholders, so security and caching headers (CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control) can be set, which GitHub Pages does not allow.

Limits:
- Headers apply only to files Netlify serves from its own store, not to proxied content or function responses.
- They are global across deploy contexts.
- Some header names are ignored, for example Content-Length, Server, Location and Set-Cookie.
- Basic-auth password headers are Pro/Enterprise only.

New Free projects get an edge-injected 'Powered by Netlify' badge script. A CSP without 'unsafe-inline' in script-src blocks it, and nothing else on the site is affected (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/projects/powered-by-netlify-badge/).

apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.answer:
Yes. Both elbcar-detailing.de and www work while DNS stays at GoDaddy, and no nameserver move is needed.

- www: CNAME www -> <project>.netlify.app. Today it points to mashreghal.github.io.
- Apex: Netlify prefers an ALIAS, ANAME or flattened CNAME record pointing to apex-loadbalancer.netlify.com. Whether GoDaddy's DNS offers those record types is not confirmed. The documented fallback works with any provider: replace the four GitHub A records (185.199.108-111.153, checked today; no AAAA records exist) with one A record @ -> 75.2.60.5.
- Redirect: Netlify adds both names automatically, and "If you set the `www` subdomain as your primary domain, Netlify will automatically redirect the apex domain to the `www` subdomain."
- Primary domain: for external DNS Netlify says "we strongly recommend setting the `www` subdomain (or another subdomain) as your primary domain". That matches today's setup with www as primary (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/domains/manage-domains/manage-multiple-domains/).
- HTTPS: a free Let's Encrypt certificate covers both names. It can only be issued once DNS points to Netlify ("this step cannot be completed until the DNS records for your custom domain are pointing to our servers", https://docs.netlify.com/manage/domains/troubleshooting-tips/), so expect a short HTTPS gap at cutover.
- Netlify DNS (a nameserver move) is only required for an apex primary domain or for branch subdomains.
apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.quote: If your DNS provider does not support ALIAS, ANAME, or flattened CNAME records, use this fallback option. ... Add an A record. Depending on your provider, leave the host field empty or enter @. ... Point the record to Netlify's load balancer IP address: 75.2.60.5.

serverless_for_form.answer:
Functions:
- Available on Free. Compute is metered: "Compute consumes 10 credits per GB-hour". Defaults are 1024 MB memory and a 60-second synchronous limit.
- Region: "By default, Netlify deploys functions for new sites to `cmh` (Ohio)". Changing it (for example fra EU Frankfurt, dub Ireland, lhr London) is "available on all Pro and Enterprise plans" only. On Free or Personal, a form function runs in the US (https://docs.netlify.com/build/functions/configuration/).

Built-in Netlify Forms:
- Price: "For credit-based plans, Forms are free and unlimited." Each submission cost 1 credit until April 14, 2026.
- Setup: add data-netlify="true" to the HTML form. Submitting via fetch (AJAX) works.
- Features: email, webhook and Slack notifications, CSV export, honeypot and reCAPTCHA. "The form request has a maximum size limit of 8 MB."

Where the data is stored:
- The docs say only: "Form submission data is securely stored in our user database." They give no region.
- Netlify staff on Netlify's official forum: "we store form submissions with our backing store(s) ONLY ... At present, that is in the US" (2021, https://answers.netlify.com/t/netlify-forms-data-center-location/24588). And: "Netlify's infrastructure is primarily hosted in the United States, so personal data handled through your form submissions would indeed be transferred there" (2024, https://answers.netlify.com/t/privacy-policy-where-does-netlify-store-form-data/128605).
- "All form submissions are filtered for spam using Akismet". Akismet is run by Automattic Inc. (US), which I found as an active participant on the official DPF list (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/forms/spam-filters/).

Conclusion: Netlify Forms would replace Formspree (not on the DPF list) with a processor that is DPF-certified and covered by a DPA. It is still not an EU-located form handler.

facts.migration_effort_from_github_pages:
Low: about 2-4 hours of work plus DNS and TLS propagation (my estimate). The site is plain static HTML/CSS/JS with no Liquid tags or front matter, so Netlify needs no build command.

Steps:
1. Sign up with the GitHub account. This links the commit identity so private-repo pushes are recognized. Install the Netlify GitHub App for this one repo only. Leave the build command empty.
2. Choose a publish directory that leaves out TODO.md and the README.md files. Today Jekyll's `exclude` in _config.yml hides them, but Netlify deploys everything in the publish directory ("Only files in the publish directory are deployed"). Either move the site into a subfolder or move the notes out.
3. Turn off the Powered-by-Netlify badge. Optionally add a `_headers` file (CSP, HSTS, caching). The existing 404.html works as is: "If you add a `404.html` page to your site, it will be picked up and displayed automatically for any failed paths." The CNAME file is no longer needed.
4. Run the first production deploy and check it on <project>.netlify.app. Then make the project public, because new teams start with projects private.
5. Add www.elbcar-detailing.de as the primary domain; the apex is added and redirected to www automatically. At GoDaddy, replace the four GitHub A records with A @ 75.2.60.5 and repoint the www CNAME to <project>.netlify.app. Wait for the Let's Encrypt certificate.
6. Disable GitHub Pages and make the repo private. A private personal repo works on Free.
7. Contact form, optional: Formspree keeps working unchanged. To switch to Netlify Forms:
   - add data-netlify="true", a name and a form-name field;
   - replace the Formspree fields (_subject, _gotcha, _replyto) with a subject input, netlify-honeypot and an `email` field (used as Reply-to);
   - change main.js, which today sends FormData to formspree.io with Accept: application/json, to POST to "/";
   - enable form detection and an email notification to the Gmail address;
   - update datenschutz.html: hosting changes from GitHub to Netlify, and the form processors become Netlify and Akismet on a DPF basis.
8. New workflow: work in pull requests, whose previews are free. Each merge to main costs 15 credits.
risks_or_gotchas: A hard cap means an outage, not a bill. If Free's 300 credits run out, the live business site and every other project on the account show "Site not available" until the next billing cycle, unless the account is upgraded. Free cannot buy extra credits. (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/accounts-and-billing/billing/billing-for-credit-based-plans/how-credits-work/)

Deploy frequency is the real cost driver. One production deploy (15 credits) uses 5% of the monthly Free budget. With 54 main-branch commits in April 2026, Free would be exceeded if each push deployed. Staying on Free needs batched PR merges, [skip netlify] in commit messages, or locked auto-publishing; otherwise use Personal at $9/month.

Free-tier terms are discretionary: "Netlify may shut down Free Usage Tier website projects without notice for any reason or no reason. In case of any delays or performance problems including those caused by a malicious attack on a website project, for the Free Usage Tier Netlify will resolve the issue by shutting down the affected website projects." There is no SLA, and liability is capped at the lesser of that month's fees or US$100. (Self-Serve Subscription Agreement sections 6 and 10)

Pricing has changed twice in about 7 months. The April 14, 2026 update doubled bandwidth (10 to 20 credits per GB) and compute (5 to 10 credits per GB-hour), while making forms free (https://www.netlify.com/changelog/2026-04-14-pricing-updates-april-2026/). Pro went from "Pro plan: $20/month with 5,000 credits" in the Sept 2025 launch blog (https://www.netlify.com/blog/new-pricing-credits/) to "Starts at $20/month for 3,000 credits" today.

Internal notes would go live. The repo relies on Jekyll's `exclude` to hide TODO.md and the README.md files. Netlify ignores _config.yml, so with the repo root as the publish directory those notes would be published, which is exactly the exposure the owner wants to end. Move the site into a subfolder or move the notes out.

The data stays in the US. Hosting, form storage and Akismet spam filtering are all in the US. Moving to Netlify Forms still improves on Formspree, because Netlify and Automattic are both active DPF participants and a DPA applies, but it is not an EU form handler. An EU function region needs Pro. Netlify's DPF recertification is due 12/17/2026.

Netlify injects scripts at the edge. Every visitor to a new public Free project sees the "Powered by Netlify" badge ("invites them to build a project of their own") until it is switched off per project. While a project is private, Netlify also injects a pre-launch toolbar.

New teams default to private projects: "Teams created on or after July 28, 2026 start with this default setting: Private for new projects". The site must be made public after the first production deploy, and "A private project isn't reachable by unauthenticated requests", which also blocks forms and webhooks. (https://docs.netlify.com/manage/security/secure-access-to-sites/project-visibility/)

Private-repo deploys run only for recognized authors. On Free and Personal that means the Team Owner's linked GitHub account; commits from any other identity wait for approval, and Git Contributors require Pro.

Cutover details: the apex A record points to one load-balancer IP, so "the apex domain can't take advantage of direct DNS routing on a global CDN". With www as primary, the apex only redirects. The certificate is issued only after DNS points to Netlify and old TTLs have expired, so plan a short HTTPS gap.

Netlify's docs contradict each other on Reviewers for Free. The pricing FAQ says "With any plan, you can add unlimited free Reviewer roles", but the roles doc says credit plans need Pro to invite Reviewers. Assume previews are owner-only, or make them public.
Reusing a Netlify account created before Sept 4, 2025 keeps it on a Legacy plan with different limits, and "Switching to Credit-based plans is irreversible".

Self-Serve Agreement section 16: "Customer grants Netlify the right to use Customer's company name and logo as a reference for marketing or promotional purposes". Section 14 lets the customer opt out of the customer list by written notice.
