- Form emails: sending to the owner's own verified Gmail address is free: "Sends to verified destination addresses are free and do not count toward the included quota." (https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/platform/pricing/)
- Spam check: Turnstile Free is free, "Up to 20 widgets", with unlimited challenges.
- Only optional cost: sending to arbitrary recipients, such as an auto-reply to the customer, needs Workers Paid. That is "a minimum charge of $5 USD per month for an account" and includes "3,000 included per month, then $0.35 per 1,000 emails".
- The domain registration stays at GoDaddy, so its cost does not change.

private_repo_on_free_tier.answer: Yes for Cloudflare Pages. The Pages docs say private GitHub repositories are supported, and the Pages overview says "Available on all plans". For Workers Builds, which connects a repo to Workers, this is not confirmed: the docs use the same GitHub app ("The GitHub App is named Cloudflare Workers and Pages, and it is shared between Workers and Pages projects.") but never say private repos are supported.
private_repo_on_free_tier.quote: You can select a GitHub project from your personal account or an organization you have given Pages access to. This allows you to choose a GitHub repository to deploy using Pages. Both private and public repositories are supported.

preview_deployments.answer:
Yes, created automatically.

Pages:
- "Every time you open a new pull request on your GitHub repository, Cloudflare Pages will create a unique preview URL, which will stay updated as you continue to push new commits to the branch."
- Each branch push gets a preview at <hash>.<project>.pages.dev, plus a branch alias such as development.<project>.pages.dev.
- "You can have an unlimited number of preview deployments active on your project at a time." This is on the Free plan.
- Previews send "X-Robots-Tag: noindex", so search engines skip them.
- "By default, these deployment URLs are public." Locking them needs Cloudflare Access ("Enable access policy"). The Zero Trust setup asks for payment details even on the free plan: "this step is still needed but you will not be charged."
- "preview URLs will not be created for pull requests created from forks of your repository."

Workers equivalent (Worker Previews):
- Turned on with Workers Builds "Enable Preview Builds".
- URL format: <preview-name>-<worker-name>.<subdomain>.workers.dev. A comment with the Preview URL is posted on the pull request.
- Free plan limit: 100 Previews per Worker.
- "Preview URLs are public by default". The workers.dev preview URLs carry X-Robots-Tag: noindex.
- "Worker Previews requires Wrangler 4.135.0 or later."

Workers docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/

custom_http_headers.answer:
Yes. Both Pages and Workers static assets read a plain-text `_headers` file, created "in the static asset directory of your project". "Headers defined in the `_headers` file override what Cloudflare ordinarily sends."
- Limits: "You may define up to 100 header rules. Each line in the `_headers` file has a 2,000 character limit."
- Default headers can be removed with "! Header-Name".
- Caveat: "Custom headers defined in the `_headers` file are not applied to responses generated by Pages Functions". The same applies to Worker code, so the form endpoint must set its own headers.
- Pages adds some headers by default, including "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *", "Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin" and "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff" (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/serving-pages/).
- `_redirects` is also supported, with up to 2,000 static and 100 dynamic redirects.

Workers docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/

apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.answer:
www can work with DNS at GoDaddy. The apex (elbcar-detailing.de) cannot.

www: only Pages can do this. You add a CNAME at GoDaddy (www → <project>.pages.dev) after adding the domain in the Pages dashboard. Adding the CNAME alone gives a 522 error.

Apex: it cannot be attached to Pages while DNS stays at GoDaddy.
- Pages requires the apex to be a Cloudflare zone, with the domain's nameservers pointed to Cloudflare.
- The docs offer no A-record or IP-address option.
- An ALIAS (flattening) record at GoDaddy would not meet the requirement: "that custom domain must be a zone on the Cloudflare account you have created your Pages project on".
- The setup that keeps an outside DNS host is not available on Free: "A CNAME setup (partial) is only available to customers on a Business or Enterprise plan."

Workers static assets cannot use GoDaddy DNS even for www. "To add a Custom Domain, you must have: An active Cloudflare zone". The compatibility matrix lists "Custom domains outside Cloudflare zones" as not supported on Workers and supported on Pages.

So serving both apex and www from Cloudflare means changing the nameservers at GoDaddy (today ns35/ns36.domaincontrol.com) to the two Cloudflare assigns on the Free plan. GoDaddy stays the registrar; Cloudflare's setup guide even links GoDaddy's "change nameservers" help page. DNSSEC is not active today (no DS record found on 2026-10-18), so the "turn off DNSSEC" step does not apply.

Partial workaround without moving DNS: Pages on www, plus GoDaddy forwarding of the apex with a 301 redirect to https://www. GoDaddy's help page (German) says "Die Weiterleitung über HTTPS wird jetzt automatisch auf Ihre Domain angewendet" (forwarding over HTTPS is now applied to your domain automatically) and "Wenn Sie eine Weiterleitung hinzufügen, wird Ihr @-A-Record automatisch aktualisiert und gesperrt" (adding a forward automatically updates and locks your @ A record). This is GoDaddy's claim and was not tested (https://www.godaddy.com/de/help/meine-godaddy-domain-weiterleiten-12123).
apex_domain_with_godaddy_dns.quote: If you are deploying to an apex domain (for example, `example.com`), then you will need to add your site as a Cloudflare zone and configure your nameservers. ... If you are deploying to a subdomain, it is not necessary for your site to be a Cloudflare zone.

serverless_for_form.answer:
Functions on the free plan: yes. Pages Functions and Workers share the Workers Free quota: "100,000 per day" requests and "10 milliseconds of CPU time per invocation". "Requests to your Pages Functions count towards your quota for the Workers Free plan."

EU region choice: no.
- "By default, Workers and Pages Functions run in a data center closest to where the request was received."
- Keeping processing inside the EU (Regional Services) is part of the Data Localization Suite, an "Enterprise-only paid add-on".
- Only storage can be pinned to the EU: a D1 database can be created with jurisdiction "eu" (the docs list no plan restriction), and "Jurisdictional Restrictions guarantee objects in a bucket are stored within a specific jurisdiction" for R2.

Built-in form handling: none. "Cloudflare does not support Netlify's Forms feature." You would write a small POST handler, and Turnstile (free) can block spam.

Email sending (Cloudflare Email Service, `send_email` binding in a Worker):
- "Sending to verified destination addresses in your account is free on all plans, including when only Email Routing is configured."
- "Sending to arbitrary recipients requires the Workers Paid plan." Email Sending to arbitrary recipients is labelled "Beta".
- "You must be using Cloudflare DNS to use Email Service."
- Setup adds MX, SPF and DKIM records on the root domain ("Cannot use Email Routing with external mail servers"). The domain has no MX records today, so nothing would clash.
- The email binding works in Workers but not in Pages Functions (compatibility matrix: Email Workers supported on Workers, not on Pages).
- The Email Service terms allow only transactional email from domains you own.

Data storage: Cloudflare stores nothing by default. The message is passed on to the owner's Gmail: "Cloudflare does not provide durable storage or 'Inbox' services".

data_protection.company_and_hq: Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. It is the contracting party for self-serve accounts: "The Service is offered by Cloudflare, Inc., located at 101 Townsend St., San Francisco, California 94107." (Self-Serve Subscription Agreement §20). The agreement is governed by California law with binding arbitration. For a company headquartered in the EU with an EU billing address, the EU Data Act Addendum also applies (§18.1). The privacy policy lists EU subsidiaries, such as Cloudflare Germany GmbH in München and Cloudflare Portugal, but the company receiving the data under the DPA is Cloudflare, Inc.
data_protection.dpf_active:
Yes, active.
- Source: the official DPF list (https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list), Active Participants tab, searched for the exact name "Cloudflare, Inc." on 2026-10-18.
- Result: "Displaying 1 to 1 of 1 participants (filtered from total of 3681 participants)": "Cloudflare, Inc.", San Francisco, CA.
- Status: the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and the UK Extension each read "Active - Re-certification under Review". Covered data: "HR Data" and "Non-HR Data".
- Screenshot: [local evidence file, not kept] Cloudflare's privacy policy (effective November 4, 2025) agrees: "Cloudflare complies with the EU-U.S. DPF, the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and the Swiss-U.S. DPF as set forth by the U.S. Department of Commerce."
data_protection.dpa_available:
Yes. It applies automatically to self-serve accounts, including free ones, with no signature needed.
- Self-Serve Subscription Agreement §6.1: "...Cloudflare will handle such Personal Data in compliance with Cloudflare's Data Processing Addendum ('Data Processing Addendum'), which is hereby incorporated by reference into this Agreement."
- DPA Version 6.4, effective April 3, 2026: "This Data Processing Addendum, including the appendices (the 'DPA'), forms part of the Main Agreement."
- DPA §6.4 relies on the DPF: "transfers of Customer Data to Cloudflare made under the Data Privacy Framework shall not be a Restricted Transfer". If the certification lapses, the EU standard contractual clauses (SCCs, 2021/914) apply instead.
- Subcontractors are listed at https://www.cloudflare.com/gdpr/subprocessors/, with 30 days' notice of changes.
data_protection.eu_data_location:
There is no EU-only option for this setup on Free or other self-serve plans.
- Static files are served worldwide: "requests for these assets are routed efficiently to locations closest to your users".
- Functions and Workers "run in a data center closest to where the request was received".
- Restricting decryption and processing to the EU, including "Running Cloudflare Workers scripts", is Regional Services in the Data Localization Suite: "Enterprise-only paid add-on".
- Cookies only come into play if bot features are switched on. Then: "By default, cookie data may be processed in Cloudflare's data center in the United States".
- Only storage can be pinned. A D1 database with jurisdiction "eu" will "only run and store data within a region", and R2 buckets can have an "eu" jurisdictional restriction. Jurisdiction restrictions for Workers KV are "not supported today".
- The transfer to the US is covered by the DPF certification plus the DPA.

notable_limits: Pages Free builds: 500 builds per month, "1 build at a time", "Builds will timeout after 20 minutes." (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/)

Pages Free size: "Cloudflare Pages sites can contain up to 20,000 files on the Free plan." "The maximum file size for a single Cloudflare Pages site asset is 25 MiB." Also 100 custom domains per project and "a limit of 100 projects per account".
Pages previews: "You can have an unlimited number of preview deployments active on your project at a time."
`_headers`: 100 rules, 2,000 characters per line. `_redirects`: "2,000 static redirects and 100 dynamic redirects". Same for Pages and Workers.

Workers Free: 100,000 requests per day to Worker code (static asset requests are free and unlimited), 10 ms CPU per invocation, 50 subrequests per request, 20,000 static asset files per Worker version, 25 MiB per file, 100 Workers per account. Over the daily limit, "Cloudflare returns Error 1027". (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)
Workers Builds Free: 3,000 build minutes per month, 1 concurrent build, 20-minute timeout. Worker Previews: 100 Previews per Worker and 100 deployments per Preview on Free.

Email Service: sends to verified destination addresses are free and outside all quotas. Arbitrary recipients only on Workers Paid ("3,000 included per month, then $0.35 per 1,000 emails"). Up to 50 recipients and 5 MiB per message (25 MiB to verified destinations), 200 destination addresses per account.
Redirects on Free: Single Redirects allow 10 rules per zone. Bulk Redirects allow 15 rules, 5 lists and 10,000 URL redirects.
Turnstile Free: "Up to 20 widgets", unlimited challenges, 10 hostnames per widget.
Partial (CNAME) DNS setup, which keeps GoDaddy as the DNS host: Business or Enterprise plan only.
facts.migration_effort_from_github_pages:
Low to moderate: roughly half a day plus waiting for DNS to propagate. No build step is needed.
1. Connect the GitHub repo. After that the repo can be made private for Pages; for Workers Builds, private-repo support is not documented.
   - Pages: no framework preset. "If you do not need a build step, leave the **Build command** field blank." Set the output folder to the folder that holds the site.
   - Workers: add a wrangler.jsonc file with the asset folder, not_found_handling "404-page", html_handling and workers_dev false. If the repo has no config file, Workers Builds' automatic setup "create[s] a pull request" to add one.
2. Keep internal notes off the web. GitHub Pages hides TODO.md, README.md, images/README.md and fonts/README.md through the exclude list in Jekyll's _config.yml, and Cloudflare ignores that file. Either move the public files into a subfolder such as public/ or add a .assetsignore file (Workers only). Also leave _config.yml and CNAME out of the published folder.
3. Fix the .html URLs. Both Pages and Workers (with default settings) redirect /impressum.html and /datenschutz.html. Update the canonical tags, sitemap.xml and internal links (index.html#…, impressum.html, datenschutz.html), or set html_handling "none" on Workers.
   - The existing top-level 404.html is used automatically by Pages. Without it, Pages would treat the site as a single-page app and serve the home page for unknown paths.
4. Add a _headers file for security headers.
5. Move DNS. Add a free Cloudflare zone and check the imported records, keeping the google-site-verification TXT record (there are no MX records and no DNSSEC today). Remove the old www CNAME to mashreghal.github.io, switch the nameservers at GoDaddy, attach www, and add a rule redirecting the apex to www.
6. Replace the form. Swap the Formspree endpoint for a small Worker endpoint with Turnstile that sends via send_email to the verified Gmail address. This needs Email Routing set up on the domain. Update the Datenschutzerklärung: Formspree out, Cloudflare in as processor.
7. Turn off GitHub Pages after the switch.

If DNS must stay at GoDaddy, only the Pages route works (www via CNAME, apex via GoDaddy forwarding). In that case Cloudflare Email Service is not available for the form.
risks_or_gotchas: Pages gets no new features. The docs say "Start new projects with Workers." Cloudflare's blog (April 8, 2025): "Cloudflare Pages will continue to be supported, but, going forward, all of our investment, optimizations, and feature work will be dedicated to improving Workers." I found no end-of-life date.

The apex needs the nameservers moved to Cloudflare, and Workers needs that even for www. DNS records are then managed at Cloudflare, not GoDaddy. "Since the quick scan is not guaranteed to find all existing DNS records, you need to review your records". The google-site-verification TXT record that Search Console needs must survive the move.
Workers custom domains: "You cannot create a Custom Domain on a hostname with an existing CNAME DNS record". The imported www → mashreghal.github.io CNAME must be deleted first.

Old .html URLs get redirected. Pages "will also redirect HTML pages to their extension-less counterparts: for instance, `/contact.html` will be redirected to `/contact`". Workers' default setting answers "/file.html" with "307 to /file". The site's canonical tags, sitemap and internal links all use .html URLs.

Internal notes would be published by mistake. Today's Jekyll _config.yml exclude list (TODO.md, README.md and others) has no effect on Cloudflare. Pages publishes the whole output folder ("The content of this directory is uploaded to Cloudflare Pages as your website's content."). Workers needs a .assetsignore file ("Wrangler will not upload asset files that match lines in this file.").

The live site also answers on <project>.pages.dev or *.workers.dev, and those addresses are not marked noindex (only previews are), so search engines could index the site twice. Fix it with a Bulk Redirect (Pages) or "workers_dev": false (Workers).
Preview URLs are public by default. Protecting them with Cloudflare Access needs the Zero Trust setup, which asks for payment details even on the Free plan (not charged).

Form email is free only to verified destination addresses. Sending to arbitrary recipients is Beta and needs Workers Paid. For Email Routing, Cloudflare "does not have an SLA" and "reserves the right to modify or discontinue Cloudflare Email Routing at any time". Emails sent through the binding "appear in the Email Routing summary as dropped, even when they were delivered successfully."
The email binding works in Workers but not in Pages Functions. A Pages-only site would need a separate Worker or an outside mail service for the form.
Free services can end "in our sole discretion" (Self-Serve Subscription Agreement §2.6). The contract falls under California law with binding arbitration.
Cloudflare's DPF status reads "Active - Re-certification under Review". If the certification lapsed, the DPA switches to the EU standard contractual clauses (SCCs) (§6.4).
Workers Free allows 10 ms of CPU per request and returns Error 1027 after 100,000 requests per day to Worker code. Only the form endpoint counts toward that; static files are unlimited.

If Bot Fight Mode is switched on, Cloudflare sets the __cf_bm cookie, and "Cloudflare encourages our customers to disclose the use of these cookies". Keep it off or mention it in the Datenschutzerklärung.
Git lock-in: "If you deploy using the Git integration, you cannot switch to Direct Upload later." (Pages)
